Positives:

• Great graphics: The game has some of the best graphics out there. Looks amazing

• Killer melee and gun combat: Both melee and gun combat feel smooth and badass. 

• Good voice acting: The voice acting is well done and fits the game.

• Nice music and sound: The music and overall sound are good. Some sounds could be boomier but still sounds great and the soundtracks are actually dope as hell. Love it.

• Decent story: The story is solid as hell. Not too long and not too short. Hits the spot.

• Good performance: The game ran smoothly for me. But doesnt seem to be the case for everybody. Take more time to optimize...

• Addictive gameplay: The game is very engaging and hard to put down.

• Great atmosphere: The game feels like a real war with so many enemies around and it fun when you dont get your @$$ beaten.

• Fun co-op: Playing with friends is a lot of fun.

• No nonsense, just pure action: The game is simple and fun, without any unnecessary complications.

• Awesome level design: The levels are well-designed and keep things interesting. Huge as hell buildings and a lot of insane scenerys.

• Good coop progression system: Perktree and gun progression is well made and grindy. I would love more but im not too sure if it would even fit the games style.


Negatives:

• No ultrawide support on release: Cmon bro just release it with ultrawide support. I know its getting patched in within release month but im already done with the story and im already gonna be done with the majority of the coop grind while playing it with huge black bars on the sides. I have played indie game alphas that already have ultrawide support.

•  No matchmaking for coop: Cmon man. I dont wanna start a max difficulty coop mission and having to pray for randoms to join my lobby or be stuck with bots. Give us coop matchmaking. At least you keep your squad after the mission ends.

• Zoanthropes: Get the hell outta here. You guys suck.

I've been gaming for a long time, and for the first time In 10+ years, I've felt the need to write a review. I won't bore you with a 5 page speech, but I have to be honest when I say that this game single highhandedly restored my faith in story mode driven games. This was rushed, and far from perfect, but it captures what makes a linear game exciting, a challenge. Playing on hard difficulty had me die a thousand times, but I kept getting back up because I love it. It's what every male game wants, a good story, great characters and it focuses on what we want, fighting an eternal war with our brothers FOR THE EMPEROR!

I really wish there was a neutral option instead of like/dislike, because I find myself not loving this game, but not hating it, either.

Pros of this game:
- It's Warhammer 40k, which if you love anything about 40k, makes it automatically awesome.
- You can yell "for the Emperor!" at 2am an wake up everyone sleeping in your house and not care they're awake, because cleansing the xenos scum from the galaxy never rests.
- You get to kill everything in graphic an entertaining ways.
- It is beautiful to look at
-You can choose from a lot of the lore chapters and really get some cool customization for your genetically modified uberhuman

Cons of this game:
-The campaign seems short
-There are annoying bugs that show up at terrible times
-After the campaign, the Operations mode gets rather formulaic and repetitive.  Still fun, but very limited in variety.
-PVP is fun for a short time, then you just get annoyed with the lack of anything other than "ooh Space Marine combat" to make it really stand out from the other more developed PVP games.

Overall, if you are obsessed or love the Warhammer 40k universe, you'll love this game because you can look past the flaws, but I would recommend you wait for it to go on sale.

Fan of the 40k universe and have put a good amount of hours into the Vermintide and Darktide games and was hopeful coming into this game. Rather than write an essay here are some summarised points of my thoughts as an average gamer with no interest in PvP.

- Game looks great in terms of visuals, performance is okay, loading times could be better.

- Difficulty scaling felt off. High difficulties punish you very quickly and doesn't leave much room for alternative play-styles. You're basically cornered into getting good at parry and dodge mechanics to survive.

- Campaign was on the shorter side but honestly felt like a slog at some stages due to the above issue when playing on the higher difficulties. Overall it was a decent story.

- Gun and sword play is satisfying. Good variety of weapons and classes on release with the options of upgrading and customising both weapons and armour via cosmetics.

- Would like to see more missions and enemy types as a priority. Gameplay loop does get very repetitive even for an average gamer who gets to play on days off.

Worth a buy? Yes. But wouldn't of regretted holding out for a cheaper price either. Glad I didn't pay to play early.

Check the forums here and on the Focus forums, I'm not the only one.

Listen, I like space fascists as much as the next guy, but this game just sucks. 

For a game that has nothing going for it but combat, it sure missed the mark. 

While the shooting feels good, the melee is light and floaty and feels like attacks pass right through enemies instead of connecting. You can try to manage hordes with ranged weapons but will inevitably get swarmed and have to resort to melee. One of the most annoying aspects of the melee combat is that you attack in the direction you are moving rather than facing. So, if you want to step back and swing your sword at the oncoming horde, too bad. You will snap in the opposite direction as soon as you attack, swinging your sword into thin air and presenting your back to the horde. I honestly don't know how this wasn't addressed in development. Dodge is useless except for the telegraphed unblockable attacks by some enemies. And all the while you are swarmed, there are ranged enemies hitting with 100% accuracy from any distance. You can either try to shoot them while the horde picks at you, or let them pick at you while you chop the horde.  Either way, your armor is being whittled down and you are forced into the same repetitive loop of parry, quicktime gunshot, and quicktime execution to keep from being hit and to regenerate armor. It gets so old so fast. 

Then you come across a boss and think maybe there will be something new. Nope. You just do the same loop of parry and gun strike 15x before the execution  

The game is easy without you ever feeling powerful or like a Space Marine. Just a big clumsy oaf slowly trudging from one quicktime event to the next.   

The game looks nice, but even that is not without issues. There are big sprawling scenes with thousands of enemies pouring in that you can barely see, because despite this being a AAA release in 2024 there is no FOV slider, no ultrawide support, and the default fov is far too narrow; leaving you mostly staring at your back. I know they said they will be adding ultrawide support, but that just shows this is an unfinished and unpolished game that was not ready for release.  You also have some enemies that are so poorly designed and executed that it is shocking they were included in the final release.  The rat like enemies look like a glitch. They add nothing but clutter. 

Then there is the content, or lack of. Only a 7 hour campaign and 6x 30 minute operations. All of which feel like you are on rails with how you need to play the game. Find a sniper rifle, next clearing is all snipers. Find a flamethrower, next section is all rats. There is no thought, no strategy, no different ways to play, and once you figure out the "parry, shoot, execute loop", no skill. 

There are barely any guns (that all play about the same) which are further limited because they tried to create unique classes that are all essentially the same aside from which guns you can use. And, you can't have two of the same classes in a group.  So you want to play a certain class or use a certain gun? Better hope no one else does.

The lack of content honestly doesn't even matter. The combat is so simple, repetitive, and unsatisfying that you will tire of it far before completing all the content.  Does ripping a tyrranid in half look cool. Sure, in a trailer, or the first few times you do it. But once you realize it's just the same quicktime event/cutscene over and over it quickly becomes tedious and tiresome rather than satisfying. 

This game had a ton of potential, unfortunately it was all wasted. 5/10
